title: multiple, accept, step, list and datalist
learningObjectives: Explain multiple, accept, step, list and datalist and create accessible, secure form behaviour.

understand.concept: The multiple attribute allows more than one value or file for supported controls. accept hints which file types a file input should offer. step controls valid numeric increments, while list connects an input to datalist suggestions. These attributes guide user input but do not secure or validate uploaded content on the server.
understand.whyItMatters: A file accept hint is not a security filter, and datalist suggestions are not a required selection. Use server-side checks for uploaded files and validate numeric rules in trusted code.
understand.analogy: These attributes add options and hints to controls; they do not replace validation of the actual submitted value.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; actual validation, submission, and assistive technology behaviour follow browser and platform rules.

explain.narrative: The form offers suggestions, integer quantity steps, and multiple file selection. The server must still validate submitted files and values.

examples.code: <form><label>Tags <input name='tags' list='tag-options'></label><datalist id='tag-options'><option value='HTML'><option value='CSS'></datalist><label>Quantity <input type='number' name='qty' min='1' max='20' step='1'></label><label>Files <input type='file' name='files' accept='image/*,.pdf' multiple></label></form>
examples.explanation: The form offers suggestions, integer quantity steps, and multiple file selection. The server must still validate submitted files and values.
examples.expectedOutput: A browser-rendered form example demonstrating the HTML behaviour described.

practise.guidedTask: Add a datalist to a search field, a numeric step to a quantity field, and multiple file selection. Explain why accept is only a hint.
practise.independentTask: Build an accessible form with labels, constraints, clear errors, and a documented server-side validation plan. Test keyboard use and invalid values.
hints: Do not rely on colour or placeholder alone.
Client-side checks do not provide authorization or security.
Keep errors associated with their fields and easy to locate.

questions.prompt: Does accept guarantee that an uploaded file is safe?
questions.explanation: accept guides file selection but does not validate file safety or content.

questions.prompt: Which form approach is most reliable?
options: Accessible client feedback plus authoritative server validation
questions.answer: Accessible client feedback plus authoritative server validation
questions.explanation: Good forms combine user-friendly browser feedback with trusted server-side enforcement.
